skill.name: tilt
skill.description: Manages Tilt development environments with CLI workflows, tmux session guidance, status checks, logs, and Tiltfile reference material.
skill.summary: Guide AI agents through Tilt CLI operations and Tiltfile authoring for local Kubernetes development.
skill.author: 0xBigBoss

security_audit.summary: Static findings are markdown backticks, documented Tilt and tmux shell examples, docs links, and localhost example URLs. I found no evidence of prompt injection, hidden network exfiltration, credential access, or obfuscated behavior in SKILL.md or TILTFILE_API.md. The remaining concern is operational: users should review commands before letting an agent start, stop, or trigger local Tilt resources.

remediation.issue: Agent-executed commands can change local Tilt state.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to confirm Kubernetes context, resource names, and intended side effects before running start, stop, trigger, or down commands.

remediation.issue: The tmux session snippet derives a session name from repository paths.
remediation.suggestion: Use quoted substitutions and sanitize the session name to avoid malformed tmux targets in unusual path names.

remediation.issue: Reference examples include external extension repository URLs.
remediation.suggestion: State that users should trust and pin extension repositories before loading custom extensions.

static_findings.snippet: Tilt live-reloads aggressively. **Never suggest restarting `tilt up` or manually refreshing resource
| **Source code with `live_update`** | Files sync to container without rebuild | Just save the file
| **Source code without `live_update`** | Full image rebuild triggers automatically | Just save the
Restarting `tilt up` is required only for:
**Always run `tilt up` in a tmux session using send-keys.** This ensures:
Never run `tilt up` directly in foreground or with `run_in_background`. Always use tmux.
- Use `tilt get uiresources -o json` to query resource status programmatically
- Use `tilt get uiresource/<name> -o json` for detailed single resource state
- Use `tilt logs` with `--since`, `--tail`, `--json` flags for log retrieval
- Use `tilt trigger <resource>` to force updates when auto-reload didn't trigger
- Use `tilt wait` to block until resources reach ready state

content.value_statement: Tilt projects can be hard to inspect without restarting resources unnecessarily. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Tilt CLI checks and Tiltfile authoring.
actual_capabilities: Explains when Tilt reloads resources automatically and when a restart is needed.
Provides tmux-based commands for starting, inspecting, and stopping tilt up.
Shows Tilt CLI queries for UIResource status, logs, triggers, and wait conditions.
Summarizes Tiltfile API patterns for resources, builds, live updates, extensions, and file operations.
Includes examples for JSON log parsing and status inspection with jq.
limitations: Requires Tilt, tmux, git, jq, and related CLI tools when using command examples.
Does not validate commands against a specific project cluster, permissions, or security policy.
Can suggest commands that change local development resources or running Tilt sessions.
Reference material may lag behind upstream Tilt releases.

use_cases.title: Debug Local Resources
use_cases.description: Inspect Tilt resource status, logs, and update states before changing a running workflow.

use_cases.title: Author Tiltfiles
use_cases.description: Use documented resource, build, live update, and extension patterns while shaping a Tiltfile.

use_cases.title: Stabilize Development CI
use_cases.description: Apply Tilt wait, trigger, and CI commands to make local validation more predictable.

prompt_templates.title: Start With Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tilt skill to check my local Tilt resources. Ask for missing resource names before suggesting commands.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate Logs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tilt skill to diagnose a failing Tilt resource. Focus on recent logs, readiness, and update status.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Tiltfile Reloads
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Tiltfile with the tilt skill. Suggest safer live update, dependency, and resource ordering changes.

prompt_templates.title: Design Multi-Service Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tilt skill to plan a multi-service Tilt workflow with Kubernetes resources, local resources, probes, and manual triggers.

output_examples.input: A developer says the api resource did not update after saving a file.
output_examples.output: A status-first troubleshooting path that checks update state, waits for readiness, and reviews recent logs before considering a restart.

output_examples.input: A platform engineer wants faster Tilt feedback for a web service.
output: Recommended live update areas to inspect.
Resource dependency questions that affect rebuild timing.

output_examples.input: A team needs consistent instructions for starting Tilt in an agent session.
output_examples.output: Guidance that uses a persistent tmux session, explains how to view output, and highlights commands that change local state.

best_practices: Check resource status and recent logs before restarting Tilt.
Confirm resource names, Kubernetes context, and project conventions before running commands.
Use structured Tilt CLI output when comparing runtime and update states.
anti_patterns: Restarting Tilt for every source edit.
Running long-lived Tilt sessions in a foreground agent process.
Copying Tiltfile examples without checking paths, dependencies, and cluster permissions.

faq.question: Does this skill install Tilt?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and command patterns for environments where Tilt and related tools are already available.

faq.question: Can it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: It can instruct an AI agent to run Tilt CLI commands when the user permits tool execution.

faq.question: Does it replace Tilt documentation?
faq.answer: No. It summarizes common workflows and links to upstream references for deeper details.

faq.question: What tools does it mention?
faq.answer: It references Tilt, tmux, git, jq, rg, Kubernetes resources, and Tiltfile APIs.

faq.question: Is it only for Kubernetes projects?
faq.answer: Tilt usually supports Kubernetes-centered development, but Tiltfiles can include local resources and custom build flows.

faq.question: What should users review before use?
faq.answer: Review command effects, cluster context, resource names, and repository trust before starting or stopping services.
